historical_record.description: Completed as the Sheet Metal Workers' Hall, to a design by the architect James E. Percey and built by William Starke of Local 104, replacing the union's building at Sixth and Market destroyed earlier that year.
The hall of Sheet Metal Workers Union Local 104; Local 355, the Sheet Metal Production Workers, was listed next door at 224 Guerrero Street.
San Francisco City Landmark No. 150. Local 104 of the Sheet Metal Workers Union occupied it until 1980.
The hall's façade is sheet metal worked to look like stone, and the ground-floor shop whose rent paid for the hall above was first a liquor and cigar store.
